## Email standards and authentication

What do SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and the mail standards require?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [RFC 5321: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc5321/) | IETF | Specifies SMTP, the protocol that moves mail between servers, with its extension mechanism and use for message submission; obsoletes RFC 2821, updated by RFC 7504. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 5322: Internet Message Format](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc5322/) | IETF | Defines the syntax of an email message, its header fields and its body; it revises RFC 2822 and is updated by RFC 6854. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 7208: Sender Policy Framework (SPF) for Authorizing Use of Domains in Email, Version 1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc7208/) | IETF | Defines SPF version 1, by which a domain publishes the hosts allowed to send mail in its name and receivers check them; obsoletes RFC 4408. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 6376: DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) Signatures](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc6376/) | IETF | Defines DKIM: a signing domain takes responsibility for a message with a cryptographic signature checked against a public key in DNS; Internet Standard 76. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 9989: Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9989/) | IETF | DMARC as specified in May 2026: identifier alignment, the policy record, and actions for mail receivers and domain owners; obsoletes RFC 7489 and 9091. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 8461: SMTP MTA Strict Transport Security (MTA-STS)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8461/) | IETF | Defines MTA-STS: policy discovery through a TXT record and an HTTPS fetch, validation of MX hosts and certificates, policy application, failure reporting, and operational advice. | Standard | Free |
| [DMARC.org](https://dmarc.org/) | DMARC.org | Explains what DMARC is, why it matters, and how it works, and tracks its status, including the three May 2026 RFCs that replaced RFC 7489. | Reference | Free |
| [M3AAWG Best Practices](https://www.m3aawg.org/published-documents) | Messaging, Malware and Mobile Anti-Abuse Working Group (M3AAWG) | M3AAWG's published best practices and papers on messaging abuse, newest first, among them sender best common practices and a paper on justifying an abuse desk. | Reference | Free |
| [Email sender guidelines (Gmail)](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) | Google | Google's rules for sending mail to personal Gmail accounts: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, PTR records, TLS, spam rates, and more above 5,000 messages a day. | Reference | Free |
| [Yahoo Sender Hub: Sender Best Practices](https://senders.yahooinc.com/best-practices/) | Yahoo | Yahoo's requirements for mail sent to its domains, stricter for bulk senders: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication, low complaint rates, valid DNS, and further recommendations. | Reference | Free |
| [BIMI Group](https://bimigroup.org/) | AuthIndicators Working Group | Explains BIMI, a specification for showing a brand's logo beside mail that passes DMARC, with three starting steps and FAQs for senders and mailbox providers. | Reference | Free |

## Mail servers and delivery

How do I run and filter a mail server?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Postfix Documentation](https://www.postfix.org/documentation.html) | Wietse Venema | Index of the Postfix mail server's documentation: basic and standard configuration, TLS and SASL, content inspection, relay and access control, lookup tables, and performance tuning. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Exim documentation](https://www.exim.org/docs.html) | The Exim Maintainers | Exim's documentation index: the specification and filter specification for the current version in HTML and PDF, older versions from a list, HOWTOs, and an FAQ. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Dovecot CE documentation](https://doc.dovecot.org/latest/) | Open-Xchange GmbH | Open-Xchange's documentation for Dovecot Community Edition, the open source IMAP, POP3, LMTP, and ManageSieve server; the commercial Dovecot Pro is documented elsewhere. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Rspamd Documentation](https://docs.rspamd.com/) | Rspamd Project | Documentation for the Rspamd spam filter: its capabilities, the stages each message passes through, installation, configuration, module reference, the Lua API, and MTA integration. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Apache SpamAssassin](https://spamassassin.apache.org/) | Apache Software Foundation | Open source spam filter that scores mail using header and body tests, Bayesian filtering, and DNS blocklists; the project site carries news, downloads, and documentation. | Tool | Free |
| [mailcow: dockerized documentation](https://docs.mailcow.email/) | The Infrastructure Company GmbH | Documentation for mailcow: dockerized, an open source mail suite of Docker containers including Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd, and SOGo: system preparation, DNS, installation, updates, and backups. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Mail-in-a-Box](https://mailinabox.email/) | Joshua Tauberer | Project that sets up a mail server on a new Ubuntu machine: webmail, IMAP and SMTP, spam filtering, automatic DNS records, and Let's Encrypt certificates. | Tool | Free |
| [Exchange Server documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/exchange-server) | Microsoft | Microsoft's documentation hub for Exchange Server Subscription Edition, 2019, and 2016: what's new, system requirements, deployment, installation and upgrades, and build numbers. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## DNS standards and references

What do the DNS standards and registries say?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [RFC 1034: Domain names - concepts and facilities](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc1034/) | IETF | With RFC 1035, Internet Standard 13: DNS concepts, covering the name space, resource records, name servers, and resolvers; updated by many later RFCs. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 1035: Domain names - implementation and specification](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc1035/) | IETF | With RFC 1034, Internet Standard 13: the DNS implementation, with resource record definitions, the message format, and master files; updated by many later RFCs. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 4033: DNS Security Introduction and Requirements](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc4033/) | IETF | With RFC 4034 and 4035, the DNSSEC specification; this part defines the terms and sets out considerations for name servers, zones, resolvers, and stub resolvers. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 9499: DNS Terminology](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9499/) | IETF | Best Current Practice 219, a glossary of DNS terms by subject: names, resource records, response codes, transactions, zones, wildcards, servers and clients, registration, and DNSSEC. | Standard | Free |
| [IANA Top-Level Domains](https://www.iana.org/domains/root/db) | IANA (Public Technical Identifiers, an affiliate of ICANN) | IANA's registry of every top-level domain with its delegation details, filterable by status, type, and writing system, and downloadable in several formats. | Reference | Free |
| [IANA Domain Name System (DNS) Parameters](https://www.iana.org/assignments/dns-parameters) | IANA (Public Technical Identifiers, an affiliate of ICANN) | IANA's registries of DNS protocol values: classes, resource record types, OpCodes, RCODEs, and more, each with its registration procedure and reference RFCs. | Reference | Free |
| [How DNS Works](https://dnsimple.com/comics/how-dns-works/) | DNSimple | DNSimple's comic about a DNS lookup, told in episodes with a bonus on glue records, a video version, and translations into many languages. | Reference | Free |

| [Cloudflare DNS docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/) | Cloudflare | Cloudflare's documentation for its authoritative DNS service: DNS records, DNSSEC, nameserver options, and Internal DNS for enterprise customers. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## Lookup and test tools

How do I test a domain's mail and DNS setup from outside?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Google Admin Toolbox](https://toolbox.googleapps.com/apps/main/) | Google | Google's web tools for troubleshooting Workspace: Check MX and Dig for DNS, Messageheader for mail delivery, HAR and log analyzers, and browser debugging pages. | Online service | Free |
| [mail-tester](https://mail-tester.com/) | MAIL TESTER LLC | Spam test for outgoing mail: send a message to the address the page generates and view its score; three tests a day are free. | Online service | Freemium |
| [Learn and Test DMARC](https://www.learndmarc.com/) | URIports.com | Teaches SPF, DKIM, and DMARC three ways: mail its tester and watch each check, take a ten-question quiz, or paste headers for a visual breakdown. | Online service | Free |
| [Internet.nl](https://internet.nl/) | Dutch Internet Standards Platform | Tests a website, a mail domain, or your connection against modern Internet standards: modern addresses, signed domains, secure connections and transport, anti-phishing, and route authorisation. | Online service | Free |
| [Zonemaster](https://zonemaster.net/en/) | AFNIC and The Swedish Internet Foundation | Runs a battery of DNS tests, DNSSEC among them, on a domain name you enter, with optional settings; the source code and documentation are linked. | Online service | Free |
| [whatsmydns.net DNS Propagation Checker](https://www.whatsmydns.net/) | whatsmydns.net | Looks up a DNS record on name servers in many countries at once and maps the answers, to show how far a change has propagated. | Online service | Free |
| [dmarcian DMARC tools](https://dmarcian.com/dmarc-tools/) | dmarcian, Inc. | dmarcian's free tools, usable without an account: a domain checker, DMARC and DKIM inspectors, an SPF surveyor, a DMARC record wizard, and a header analyzer. | Online service | Free |
